To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NMDA antagonist MK801 differentially inhibits the induction of a variety of genes in dentate granular cells and hilar interneurons following a single hippocampal afterdischarge.
MK801 inhibits the induction of Fos, c-Jun, Jun-B, Jun-D, BDNF and trkB mRNA and protein by a single hippocampal afterdischarge.
MK801 significantly attenuates the expression of a subset of immediate-early gene and neurotrophine-related mRNAs induced by a single after-discharge.

the identification of those genes whose induction by kindling may be responsible for the changes in neural plasticity and connectivity which are associated with kindling development and which are likely to play a role in epileptogenesis.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying epileptogenesis.

the identification and characterization of the changes in gene expression that are produced by kindling, with the goal of determining whether the changes in gene regulation that occur during kindling are important in the kindling process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

NMDA receptor activation is necessary for the induction of a number of immediate-early and trophic factors, but that the NMDA system is not involved in the expression of all immediate-early genes induced by kindling.
MK801 inhibits those genes that are most likely to play an important part in the NMDA-dependent component of kindling development and the associated changes in neural connectivity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MK801 inhibits the induction of a number of genes whose expression is associated with kindling, and that these genes are likely candidates for a role in kindling and moss fibre sprouting.
MK801 inhibits kindling by blocking the expression of a number of genes that are likely to play an important functional role in kindling development.
MK801 differentiates between the genes induced by an AD and those that may be involved in the development of kindled behaviour and associated changes in connectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMDA receptor antagonists can be used to identify genes that are important in the development of kinding.
